title: Winter Olympics: hosts and who topped the table
intro: Every Winter Games of the last twenty years and the next two: where they were held, and which country finished top of the medal table.
dataNote: Hosts and years are not in dispute anywhere. The medal figures now come from Wikipedia's current tables, fetched by scripts/fetch-wikipedia.mjs, and every row was checked to add up before it was accepted. That changed one answer: the Sochi 2014 table is not the one from the closing ceremony. After the doping disqualifications Norway tops it on eleven golds and Russia is second on ten, so the host no longer won its own Games. Pyeongchang 2018 stays a tie on golds between Norway and Germany, with Norway ahead on total medals.

tables.title: The Games
rows: Canada — 14 golds. The United States took the most medals overall, 37
Norway — 11 golds. Russia led when the Games closed on 13; after the doping disqualifications the revised table has Russia second on 10
Norway and Germany tied on 14 golds; Norway took the most medals, 39
Norway — 18 golds and 41 medals, a record for a single Winter Games
1–17 February 2030 — not yet held, and the first Games awarded to a region rather than a city
